newsitem.title: USA: Georgia transport chief pitches gasoline tax hike.
newsitem.headline: Georgia transport chief pitches gasoline tax hike.

text.p: Georgia will fall about $12 billion short of the $30 billion needed to pay for road projects listed in its 20-year transportation plan, state Transportation Commissioner Wayne Shackelford told lawmakers.
In legislative budget hearings Thursday, Shackelford pitched his department's proposal to raise gasoline taxes by 8 cents a gallon to help fund the work.

Georgia taxes gasoline at 7.5 cents a gallon and adds 3 cents a gallon in fuel sales taxes. The increase approved by the Department of Transportation board and supported by some lawmakers would add another 8 cents, putting the total at 18.5 cents a gallon.
The state's 20-year transportation plan, which runs through 2015, calls for paving tens of thousands of miles of dirt roads and widening dozens of rural highways to four lanes.
Although the legislature annaully appropriates millions of dollars for the work, Shackelford told lawmakers, "We won't see Georgia's unpaved roads paved with this level of funding."
Gov. Zell Miller has said he will veto any tax increase, inlcuding the proposed gasoline tax hike.
